name: Deno KV
tagline: Key-value store built into the Deno runtime; its hosted backend ends with Deno Deploy in 2027.
description: Deno KV is a key-value database exposed directly in the Deno runtime as Deno.openKv(): keys are ordered tuples, values are structured-cloneable JavaScript, and atomic operations give optimistic-concurrency transactions. Locally it is backed by SQLite; on Deno Deploy it was backed by a globally replicated FoundationDB-based service, and the open-source denokv server lets you self-host it. On 9 October 2026 Deno announced its team is joining Cloudflare and that Deno Deploy will shut down six months later; the runtime gets one more year of maintenance releases. The hosted KV service therefore has an end date, and new projects should choose another store.
statusNote: Deno announced (Oct 9, 2026) its team is joining Cloudflare; Deno Deploy, the hosted KV backend, shuts down ~6 months later. Self-hosted denokv remains MIT. Consider Durable Objects or Workers KV.

pricing.notes: Local and self-hosted (denokv) use is free; hosted KV is billed through Deno Deploy until its shutdown.

scale.notes: Local/self-hosted instances are single-node SQLite; the hosted service replicated reads globally.

strengths: Zero setup: built into the Deno runtime with no dependencies
Atomic operations with versionstamp checks for optimistic transactions
Ordered tuple keys make prefix and range listing natural
Watch API for change notifications and expireIn for TTL
Self-hostable via the open-source denokv server and npm client
weaknesses: Hosted backend ends with Deno Deploy's shutdown (~April 2027)
Queues (enqueue/listenQueue) were already unsupported on the new Deno Deploy
Small values (64 KiB) and keys (2 KiB) limits
No secondary indexes or query language
useCases: Prototypes and small Deno apps needing persistence
Local development storage for Deno tools
Self-hosted denokv for existing Deno KV codebases
